subject: botany
question_text: Name two diseases caused by mycoplasma.

verification.note: Sourced from the Junior Fastrack botany book, Biological Classification chapter (book pp.4-5), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star ranks and NO year citations. Only ONE source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this card, not merely pending: 'not checked' must never be read as 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Disease in plants
steps.why: Mycoplasma are the smallest living cells and lack a cell wall; some infect plants, and witches' broom is the plant disease named in the syllabus.
common_mistakes: Writing a fungal disease such as wheat rust here. Wheat rust is caused by Puccinia, a fungus.
steps.memory_tip: One plant disease, one animal disease: witches' broom, then pleuropneumonia.
steps.margin_note: Naming the disease is enough; adding the host (plants) makes it exact.

steps.label: Disease in animals
steps.why: The second named disease completes the two the question asks for; pleuropneumonia in cattle is the animal example in the syllabus.
common_mistakes: Writing pneumonia alone. The named disease is pleuropneumonia, in cattle.
Attributing these diseases to viruses. Mycoplasma are wall-less cells, not viruses.
steps.memory_tip: Pleuro-pneumonia — the longer word is the cattle disease.
steps.margin_note: One line per disease; the spelling of pleuropneumonia matters.

insider_note: Each correctly named disease earns one mark; a misspelt pleuropneumonia is the common loss here.
